content:
The datasheet splits configuration by **ordering code** (footnotes 1 and 2). Wavelength min/max/center map to **transmit** ranges per part; receiver ranges (1440–1540 nm for -34, 1260–1360 nm for -43) are separate row labels for the same two parts, not extra orderable modes. Protocols and **100 Mbps–2.67 Gbps** appear once in the same technical block for both parts—no per-protocol or per-rate rows—so those values belong on **both** model modes. With one scalar field per parameter, **two modes** are the evidence-based grouping; pairing each `standards_code` or `bit_rate_gbps` to a single mode without a table row would be speculative.

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-MR25-BX20D-34 1310nm Tx / 1490nm Rx",
      "model": "SO-SFP-MR25-BX20D-34",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1270.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1350.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1310.0,
      "standards_code": "FE",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 0.1
    },
    {
      "label": "SO-SFP-MR25-BX20D-43 1490nm Tx / 1310nm Rx",
      "model": "SO-SFP-MR25-BX20D-43",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1470.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1510.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1490.0,
      "standards_code": "FE",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 0.1
    }
  ]
}
```

**Note:** The schema allows only one `standards_code` and one `bit_rate_gbps` per mode, while the sheet lists **13** protocols and a **0.1–2.67 Gbps** range shared by both SKUs. Assigning every pool value to distinct modes would require inferring protocol/rate pairings that the table does not give. If your pipeline expects full coverage, it likely needs array fields or a single mode object with multi-valued properties—not 26 guessed (model × protocol) rows.

**Unassigned wavelength atoms** (Rx bands): `wavelength_min_nm` 1440 / 1260 and `wavelength_max_nm` 1540 / 1360 for -34 Rx and -43 Rx—use **four** modes (Tx + Rx per model) only if Rx rows are treated as separate configurations; the ordering table treats one configuration per part number with both directions implied.
